hypothesis: Cinema openings became more geographically decentralised over time.
evidence: Later openings include north, north-east, east and west new-town/commercial nodes, while early mapped records cluster more strongly in the central/southern area.
limitation: No population denominator or complete historical address coverage; the dataset is purposive rather than a census.

hypothesis: The 1970s–1990s show a distinct new-town cinema geography.
evidence: The 1970–1989 bin has 8 mapped sites and 8 of 9 operations are community/new-town-oriented; 1990–2009 adds Yishun, Bishan, Jurong and Tampines nodes.
limitation: Three Ang Mo Kio records are medium confidence and the pilot is not a complete market inventory.

hypothesis: Later cinema development becomes more strongly associated with mall-integrated locations.
evidence: Mall-integrated operations account for 6 of 12 openings in 1990–2009 and 3 of 5 in 2010–present; mixed-use formats remain present.
limitation: Later mall cases were deliberately strengthened in sampling; venue coverage is not a population measure.

hypothesis: Some cinema sites demonstrate strong continuity despite changes in name, operator, or building form.
evidence: Six mapped sites have 2–3 documented operations, including Lido, Toa Payoh, Kong Chian/Central and Shaw Towers.
limitation: Repeated addresses are few and mainly central/new-town case studies, not a citywide spatial cluster.

hypothesis: The modern cinema geography is concentrated into fewer but larger commercial nodes.
evidence: The frozen dataset has opening records and partial screen/seat data, not a complete contemporary active-cinema census or comparable node-size measure.
limitation: Closing/current-status coverage is insufficient; no exact claims about current market concentration.
